libraryPreparationPreflight.agent_guidance: Exercise io.micronaut.core.async.publisher.Publishers and io.micronaut.core.execution.ReactiveExecutionFlow directly in plain JUnit tests (no ApplicationContext/bean context needed, unlike io.micronaut.reactor:micronaut-reactor). Focus on CompletableFuture<->Publisher and Reactor Flux/Mono conversions, since Reactor is the framework's default reactive type here; RxJava2/3 paths are reflection/classpath-gated and can be left unexercised. No Docker image, environment variable, or system property applies.
risks: Could not fetch the live 5.1.3 POM/Gradle module metadata (no network access in this environment), so the assumption that reactor-core arrives as a transitive, non-optional dependency is inferred from the module's known design and sibling-module precedent, not independently verified.

If test compilation fails on a missing io.projectreactor:reactor-core class, treat that as the concrete evidence this analysis lacked, and add it as a testImplementation dependency pinned to the version used by io.micronaut.reactor:micronaut-reactor:4.0.0 for consistency.
libraryPreparationPreflight.summary: micronaut-core-reactive exposes plain static reactive-streams utilities (Publishers, ReactiveExecutionFlow, CompletableFuturePublisher) that don't require a Micronaut ApplicationContext/DI, unlike the bean-based micronaut-reactor integration module. No Docker, network, or filesystem interaction is involved, and its Reactor-based default conversion path is expected to already come in via the artifact's own transitive dependencies.
